Stage select

Notes メモ

Music
One song plays each match. Give a stage several and one is picked at random each match; online, both players hear the same one. A stage with none plays the stage fallback from Music, or what its own .def names.
Thumbnail
The select screen shows sprite 9000,1 of the stage's own sprite file, and few stages ship one. Add thumbnail draws the stage's background into it; the file is backed up first, and Put it back restores it exactly.
Widescreen fit
A stage narrower than the build is drawn larger than its fighters in a wide fight, its height cut. The fit widens its coordinate space at the same height and pulls the camera in. It edits the stage's own .def; Undo puts it back.
Adding
Drop a stage folder, .zip, .rar, .7z or .def anywhere on this page. A bare .png or .jpg becomes a stage: you place the ground, and the .def and .sff are written for you.
Removing
✕ asks once more, then deletes the stage's files from this build, never your original copies. A build always keeps one stage.

(default music) keeps the screenpack's own track for that screen.

Notes メモ

Preview
Plays the track here, one at a time, starting at the Master level at the top of the page (remembered on this computer).
Stage fallback
The track every stage without a song of its own plays. Pick a stage's songs on the Stages page.
Removing

Staffスタッフ

Mugen Studio Version 2.0

Mugen Studio builds a MUGEN / Ikemen GO fighting game for you. Roster, stages, music, screenpack: drag it in, lay it out, export it.

  • Siteenergyjp.comthe band's home
  • GitHubenergyjp/ikemen-go-webthe browser engine fork

What it doesYou end up with a website anyone can play in a browser, or a desktop game on the official Ikemen GO. Everything lives in one folder with nothing to install: double-click MugenStudio.exe and go. It replaces the old Modding Kit.

Why it existsPutting a MUGEN build together has always meant hand-editing select.def, hunting down the files a character forgot to ship, and guessing why a stage will not load. Mugen Studio does that part, so the time goes into the roster instead of the text files.

The band バンドa click on one deals their next tip

The band rides along: click the mascot at the top of the window - WB, DJ AR or SHiZUKA, each in turn - for a tip about the page you are on, and SHiZUKA keeps an eye on things from the cover.

WBLook: WB

Writes whole, dry sentences, a few thousand years tired, and dodges questions about himself.

DJ ARLook: DJ-AR

All lower case and loud. The shades never come off.

SHiZUKALook: SHiZUKA

Does not speak, she hums. Writes in lower case, with kaomoji and a little Japanese.

♥ Pair bench

  

    
    
    
  

  

  

  

    
    
    
  

  

    How this works
    

      

        
Chips

        
Each chip is one action number the giver asks her to play. The bench only counts; it never gives a percentage.

        
Hover a chip for its details. Click it to see the sprites.

      

      

        
Letters: how he asks

        
    
          
  • G guarded: he first checks that she has her own tailored action (SelfAnimExist). If not, he falls back to something else.
    • 
          
  • A assumed: he plays her action with no check. If she does not have it, she keeps her last animation.
    • 
          
  • U unguarded: he plays his own action on her sprites (ChangeAnim2). She moves his way, drawn in her own art.
    • 
          
  • C computed: he asks for his own action number plus a fixed number, so every action of his that has a pose becomes a request. Colored like U. Her files decide which set of his actions counts.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Colors: what she shows

        
    
          
  • green It works. G and A: she has her own action. U and C: her sprite file has every frame.
    • 
          
  • amber Some frames are missing, so she is partly blank.
    • 
          
  • red No frames at all. She vanishes at that pose (U and C).
    • 
          
  • gray G and A: she has no action of her own there. U and C: it could not be checked.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Borders

        
    
          
  • double Works only because the build fills in her missing frames with frames she has, in its own copy of her sprite file. Hover to see what her own file holds.
    • 
          
  • dotted Assumed (A): nothing checks that she has it.
    • 
          
  • dashed She also plays this number herself. Same number, maybe a different move.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Scenes

        
    
          
  • A click shows one scene at a time. A number can be in many custom states, each with its own giver pose, so pick the scene.
    • 
          
  • Left: the giver's animations from his state during that scene, followed the way the engine runs them: through the handoff after a grab, with a computed TargetState worked out. Each one says how it is picked.
    • 
          
  • Right: what she shows. Her tailored action, or his action drawn with her sprites, blank where a frame is missing.
    • 
          
  • The two sit side by side. They are not placed the way the game places them.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Check it in the game

        
The match is the real test. Start Training from the menus. Then use Lock-On (Caps Lock) and the Scene Viewer (Tab) to pose a scene.

      

    

  






  
  
Colors · 

  

  

    

      

      

      
zoom1×or the mouse wheel

      

        
        

      

    

    

      

      

      

      

        

      
added in the Studio

      

    

  

  

    How this works
    

      

        
Why

        
A character’s sprites are not painted in colors. Each pixel points to one of 256 colors in a table called the palette. A new color for the character is just another table, so nothing is ever repainted.

      

      

        
Color families

        
    
          
  • Every color is sorted into a family by its hue in the palette you start from.
    • 
          
  • Each family moves on its own: turn the blues red and the skin (in the oranges) stays skin.
    • 
          
  • The top row, everything, moves all colors at once.
    • 
          
  • Hue turns a color around the color wheel. Sat makes it more vivid or grayer. Light moves it toward white or black.
    • 
          
  • Double-click a slider to set it back to 0.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Your own picks

        
    
          
  • Families can be too blunt: the whites of the eyes and a white shirt are both grays.
    • 
          
  • Click any color on the sprite to make it a pick. It leaves its family and gets its own sliders.
    • 
          
  • Set to gives a pick an exact color.
    • 
          
  • Zoom in to aim at something small, like an eye. The line under the sprite shows the color under the pointer and what a click would grab.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Grab more at once

        
    
          
  • Turn up similar colors and one click grabs the whole shaded ramp, not just one color.
    • 
          
  • Touching only spreads like a magic wand and stops at the outline. That keeps an eye apart from a shirt of the same white.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Limits

        
    
          
  • Nothing can split one color in two. If the eye and the shirt use the very same palette color, they change together. With show what a click grabs on, the checker shows this before you click.
    • 
          
  • Only sprites that use the character’s shared palette change. Effects and portraits usually keep their own colors. The panel warns you when the sprite you are previewing is one of those.
    • 
        

      

      

        
What changes

        
    
          
  • The sprite on the left changes as you drag, with the same math the build uses. What you see is what ships.
    • 
          
  • A new color takes the next free palette number (the engine reads up to 100). If the screenpack has a palette list, it shows up there under that number.
    • 
          
  • Only the build’s copy changes: a line in the shipped .def plus an .act beside it for an old-format sprite file, or a palette inside the shipped sprite file for a new-format one.
    • 
          
  • The character’s own files are never changed.
    • 
        

      

    

  






  
  
Portraits · 

  

  

  

  

    How this works
    

      

        
Why

        
The select screen shows two pictures of each character: the small cell face and the big portrait. Characters that came with this screenpack have art cut to fit it. Characters from anywhere else usually do not, and no setting can change that - only art of the right size can.

        
The pack expects is the size most of this screenpack’s own characters use, in this character’s pixels.

      

      

        
Pick the art

        
    
          
  • Any sprite in the character’s own file, or
    • 
          
  • your own picture: choose a file, or drop it on a slot. Any image your browser opens works, and transparency is kept.
    • 
        

        
The list offers group 9000, the portrait group. The groups beside it hold other art (9020 and 9021 are how a character looks after Midnight Bliss), so they are named above the slots instead of offered.

      

      

        
Fit it

        
    
          
  • Cover fills the box, cropping around the focus point.
    • 
          
  • Contain fits the whole picture inside the box.
    • 
          
  • Stretch fills the box and ignores the shape.
    • 
          
  • Crisp keeps hard pixels and exact colors when enlarging; smooth blends. Shrinking always blends.
    • 
        

      

      

        
What changes

        
    
          
  • Only this screenpack uses the fit, on the website and in the desktop export.
    • 
          
  • The character’s own files are never changed. Remove the fit and the original art comes back.
    • 
          
  • The lifebar usually shows the cell face, so it gets the fitted face too.
    • 
          
  • Your picture becomes a normal 256-color sprite with its own palette, so nothing else about the character changes. It is kept in this bundle’s portraits folder until no fit uses it.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Limits

        
    
          
  • Works with both sprite-file versions, but only indexed (256-color) art can be a source - not a truecolor sprite.
    • 
          
  • In an old-format sprite file whose portrait shares its palette with the sprites after it, your picture is matched to that palette, so its colors are close but not exact.
    • 
        

      

    

  






  
  
♪ Sounds

  

    
    
    
  

  

    

    

    

      How this works
      

        

          
The list

          
Every sound in the character's own .snd file, exactly as the file holds it. Each one is a complete WAV.

          
    
            
  • used is how many calls name the sound directly, with the file and line of the first one.
    • 
            
  • A dimmed sound has no such call. It may still play from a computed call, where the number is worked out during the match.
    • 
          

        

        

          
Play and save

          
    
            
  • ▶ plays the sound at the slider's volume (50% to start). Press it again to stop.
    • 
            
  • ⤓ saves the sound as a WAV file.
    • 
            
  • Only one sound plays at a time.
    • 
            
  • A sound loads only when you press ▶ or ⤓, and nothing is kept afterward.
    • 
          

        

        

          
In a match

          
The website plays a character's own PlaySnd at 39% volume. The desktop export plays it at full volume.

        

      

    

  

  

  

    
    
  

  

  

    How this works
    

      

        
Check

        
    
          
  • Check this character lists its missing sounds and loud lines.
    • 
          
  • Check the whole roster checks everyone, worst first. Click a row to see that character.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Missing sounds

        
Every call that asks for a sound the character's own .snd does not have:

        
    
          
  • any PlaySnd
    • 
          
  • any hitsound or guardsound with the S prefix
    • 
        

        
These play nothing, and the engine logs nothing.

      

      

        
Counted, not checked

        
    
          
  • Calls with the F prefix, which use the common fight sounds.
    • 
          
  • Computed calls like Svar(58),N, which the file alone can't answer.
    • 
        

        
So there may be more missing sounds than this shows.

      

      

        
Loud literals

        
    
          
  • volumescale of 150 or more, or the old volume of 128 or more.
    • 
          
  • A call with no prefix is capped at 39% on the website, whatever the number says. The desktop export plays it at full volume.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Sounds wrong?

        
If every call in a move is found, the sound is what the character's author chose. A voice grunt where you expected a hit is content, not a bug.

      

    

  

  






  
  
✓ Content audit

  

    
    
    
  

  

  

    How this works
    

      

        
What it checks

        
What the character's own files ask for that the engine can't find. It reads the files the way the engine does, without playing a match:

        
    
          
  • the first [Files] section
    • 
          
  • st/stN/cmd/stcommon
    • 
          
  • the engine's common states
    • 
        

      

      

        
What the results mean

        
    
          
  • Breaks: the character won't load, or a move leads to a state no loaded file defines. That parks the character in an empty state, frozen until hit.
    • 
          
  • Worth a look: often real, but tests on real characters showed it is wrong too often to call a break.
    • 
          
  • Drawn with no colors: art whose palette is black wherever it draws, so it shows as a black silhouette. The colors are missing from the files, not the code.
    • 
          
  • Also noted: everything else the check found. Not breaks.
    • 
        

      

      

        
Fixing it

        
    
          
  • Every entry names the file and line to edit. You can select and copy it.
    • 
          
  • Read that line before you change anything.
    •

Content bundles

  
Each bundle is a whole set of characters, stages, music, themes and roster, and exports to its own folders, so switching never overwrites another build. The Studio edits one at a time; the one you choose opens the next time the Studio starts.

  

  

  

    
    
  

  
  
  

    
Open a build where it is (read-only) reads it · copies nothing

    
Look through a MUGEN or Ikemen GO build and play it without copying it: its characters, stages, music and screenpack are read from its own folders, and nothing in it is ever changed. Nothing can be edited while it is open.

    

      
      
    

    

      
      
    

    

  

  
  

    
Import a MUGEN or Ikemen GO build copies it · new bundle

    
Point this at a folder you have been playing MUGEN out of - the one with the program, chars/ and data/ in it. It is read, never written to, and what it holds becomes a new bundle.

    

      
      
    

    

      
      
      
    

    

    

  




  
Enable the H-MUGEN module?

  

  
The module shows their roles, the pair bench and the H gallery, and this bundle's builds carry the gallery. Off, none of it shows and the builds leave it out.

  

    
    
    
  

  
You can change this any time in Mods → H-MUGEN module.

. The scan was not sure about these: the pictures are what it read as pair art. Your answer is kept for this bundle; Properties → H role changes it later.
